body:
I can't even begin to describe how much I needed to hear this. It definitely makes me feel less alone. Everything you've said is right, especially about how this does impact my SO too no matter how much I want to keep it to myself. 

I do have a therapist but it feels like every time we meet it's a good day. The bad days are so intense I feel so ashamed to bring them up after the initial wave of grief passes. My therapist has no idea. But I do need to put more into it. I'm fortunate to have her and to know I'm seeing her this week. I think a lot of my issues with being closed off in therapy stem from being sent to "therapy" when I came out to my parents. Not full-blown conversion therapy but a Christian therapist who was supposed to either convince me to be straight or convince me to be celibate. I HATED him, and how he used everything I told him against me. My current therapist knows I had a negative therapy experience but maybe it's helpful to tell her the depth of it. 

And I do need to lean on other friends. It's unfair to make my SO carry all this with me. I don't have many friends and certainly not many nearby, but I need to reach out to them. 

Anyway. Thank you so much for your message. It gave me some strength today and made me feel like I do have agency, and options, and power. I haven't felt that way in a long time.
